chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Abd al-Rahman and Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a woman who came to a group of men and informed them that she was free, so one of them married her and gave her the dowry of a free woman. Then her master came and said, 'She is returned to him, and her children are slaves.'

key_terms.حُرَّةٌ: Free woman (as opposed to a slave woman)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the children of a slave woman who marries a free man while claiming to be free?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled that the husband retains the slave woman as his wife, but their offspring remain slaves, illustrating the principle of 'Umm al-Walad' (mother of the child) in Shia jurisprudence. This specific case highlights the legal distinction between the woman's status at the time of marriage and the resulting lineage, a key topic in the chapter on contracts with slave women. The ruling underscores the practical application of manumission and inheritance rights within the household structure of early Islamic society.
